name: identity-workforce-access
objective: Verify and close only proven gaps in Captain authentication, role/surface authorization, Workforce lifecycle/readiness and session/device/push isolation on BB.
truthOwner: Identity authenticates role/surface/session; Workforce owns Captain profile/readiness; DSH consumes the authorized actor and must not replace either truth.

tasks.objective: Prove Captain provisioning and fail-closed readiness end to end
tasks.currentProblem: The current app already composes server-backed fail-closed readiness, but package evidence has not yet proven current Identity/Workforce provisioning, migration compatibility, suspended/missing/wrong-role denial and control-panel readback on one candidate.
tasks.requiredChange: Run current Captain, Identity and Workforce checks first; reproduce any mismatch from Captain create/activation/profile through readiness. Fix only at the owning Identity/Workforce/DSH boundary and preserve the current fail-closed gate when it is correct.
tasks.targetState: A valid Captain reaches DshCaptainSurface only with matching Identity role/surface and allowed Workforce readiness; every invalid or unavailable state remains explicit and durable across refresh/restart.
tasks.action: Trace control-panel Captain lifecycle to Identity actor and Workforce profile/readiness, execute current tests, inspect persisted/migration behavior, fix the authoritative owner only if a failing case is reproduced, then rerun all invalidated checks.
mustNotChange: Do not create a Captain-local readiness source.
Do not bypass role/surface/readiness in development production paths.
Do not rewrite historical immutable migrations; use governed forward compatibility/amendment rules.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid Captain control-panel identity/profile and app readback resolve to the same actor identity.
Current Identity migration ledger remains convergent for accepted historical digests and no applied row is destructively rewritten.
tasks.rollback: Revert the focused authoritative-owner change while preserving current migration-history compatibility; never restore a bypass or local readiness truth.
tasks.commitBoundary: One focused U002 product commit only after reproduced failure and affected checks pass.

tasks.objective: Prove session device push and mobile-runtime isolation
tasks.currentProblem: SecureStore, device fingerprint and push registration are wired, but stale-session, logout/relogin, actor-switch, restart and transport failure behavior still require evidence.
tasks.requiredChange: Exercise current Captain runtime tests and negative lifecycle scenarios; repair only proven stale binding, cross-actor readback, token lifecycle or push rebinding defects at their owner.
tasks.targetState: No local session/device/push state can authorize another Captain, survive logout incorrectly, or fabricate readiness when backend truth is unavailable.
tasks.action: Run app-captain test/runtime-contract/typecheck, inspect Identity session storage/revocation and push registration ownership, then perform device/runtime verification for restart/logout/relogin when the implementation unit reaches runtime evidence.
mustNotChange: Do not log tokens or sensitive device identifiers.
Do not use device fingerprint as server authorization.
Do not weaken backend role/surface/actor checks to make a local test pass.
acceptanceCriteria: Logout/relogin/restart cannot expose another Captain's protected state.
Push registration is rebound/revoked according to authenticated actor/surface lifecycle.
Runtime transport errors fail explicitly rather than silently granting readiness.
tasks.rollback: Revert only the focused session/push fix; do not restore insecure persistence or a role/readiness bypass.
tasks.commitBoundary: Keep session/device/push fixes in the U002 boundary and rerun the full app-captain runtime test command.
